intent: Review the cumulative Linux sharing implementation and its memory optimizations: four capture/clipboard actions, configurable S3 uploads and naming, local archives, history, CLI/MCP, native Cinnamon/GNOME/KDE integration, and a lightweight resident with transient graphical helpers. Preserve approved behavior and durable operation semantics. Verify local memory claims while explicitly retaining pending current live-S3 and full release acceptance gates.

actionable_findings.title: Per-item checkpoints rewrite every history row in the batch
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: Sharing a multi-file clipboard batch performs quadratic journal work, including on the local-only path. OperationService saves the whole operation after each archived item, name check, and upload transition, while each save executes two lookups and an upsert for every item: the default permitted 100-file local batch alone performs roughly 30,000 history statements during its archive checkpoints. This unnecessary work delays completion and occupies the bounded operation worker; the supported 10,000-file configuration magnifies it to roughly 300 million statements for that phase alone.
actionable_findings.validation_reason: For an admitted multi-file local batch, OperationService.cpp:178 checkpoints after each archived item through :169 and HistoryStore.cpp:58-68 performs three history statements per item on every checkpoint, yielding quadratic ledger work under Settings.h:22 and Settings.cpp:154 limits without a changed-item guard; wall-clock incidence and speedup were not measured.
